title: How Long an Allowance Stands on a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card
content:
An allowance loaded onto a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card does not always die with the benefit period it was loaded for. How long it stands is settled by the card's carry-forward term, the basis its allowance is loaded on, and how many loads the card has taken.

**The rule.** An allowance stands to the last day of the benefit period after the one it was loaded for, where the card lets an unspent allowance carry into the next period, its allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year and at least 2 loads have been made to it; it stands to the last day of the benefit year, where the card lets an unspent allowance carry into the next period, its allowance is loaded on calendar months of the benefit year and at least 2 loads have been made to it; and it stands only to the last day of the benefit period it was loaded for in every other case.

**The three conditions in combination.**

| Unspent allowance carries into the next period | Allowance loaded on | Loads made to the card | An allowance stands |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | calendar quarters of the benefit year | 2 or more | to the last day of the benefit period after the one it was loaded for |
| yes | calendar months of the benefit year | 2 or more | to the last day of the benefit year |
| yes | either basis | fewer than 2 | only to the last day of the benefit period it was loaded for |
| no | either basis | any number | only to the last day of the benefit period it was loaded for |

The loads made to the card are counted from the card's own scheduled load entries, across the record as a whole and not only within one period.

**How the further benefit periods are counted.** Where the card lets an unspent allowance carry into the next period, its allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year and at least 2 loads have been made to it, an allowance stands for 1 further benefit period. Where the card lets an unspent allowance carry into the next period, its allowance is loaded on calendar months of the benefit year and at least 2 loads have been made to it, the further benefit periods an allowance stands for are 3 less the benefit periods of the year that have already passed. In every other case an allowance stands for no further benefit period.

**Worked illustrations, on hypothetical cards.** A card that carries an unspent allowance forward, is loaded on calendar quarters and shows three scheduled loads: an allowance stands one further benefit period beyond the one it was loaded for. A card on the same terms showing a single load: fewer than 2 loads have been made, so an allowance stands only to the last day of its own period. A card whose term carries nothing forward: whatever basis its allowance is loaded on and however many loads it shows, an allowance stands only to the last day of the benefit period it was loaded for.
